topic: Correcting the measured rate of the r5 domain-guard TOCTOU race
theFindingIsREAL: The r5 reviewer's core claim is correct and independently confirmed: limiter.guard_window_domain checked EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM limiter.bucket) with no lock, so it could not see a concurrent uncommitted admission, and a window_seconds change could slip through leaving an old-domain row stranded.

measurementCorrection.whatBothPartiesFirstMeasured: The reviewer reported 30/30, and the author's first reproduction also returned 30/30. BOTH used the hit condition 'window_seconds changed AND limiter.bucket is non-empty'.
measurementCorrection.whyThatIsWrong: A row created AFTER the change, under the NEW domain, is correct behaviour. Counting it inflates the rate to ~100%.
measurementCorrection.correctedHitCondition: window_seconds changed AND a surviving row's window_id belongs to the OLD domain, i.e. window_id = window_of(now(), old_window_seconds).

correctedRates.unlockedControl_deterministicHeldTransac: REPRODUCED - the config change was accepted with no error and left 1 stranded old-domain row
correctedRates.fixed_deterministicHeldTransaction: REFUSED - the change waits on the advisory lock, then correctly sees the row and RAISES; window_seconds unchanged, no stranded row

measurementCorrection.conclusion: The defect is real and the deterministic case proves the window exists. Its NATURAL incidence is roughly 1 in 30 under this two-process test, not 30 in 30. Stating 30/30 would overstate the measured severity, so it is corrected here rather than repeated.

fix.mechanism: limiter.domain_lock_key() names one advisory key. Every admission takes pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared for its whole transaction; a window_seconds change takes pg_advisory_xact_lock (exclusive) before checking.
fix.whyItCloses: Shared does not conflict with shared, so admissions never serialise against one another. A domain change waits for every in-flight admission to finish, and while it holds the lock no new admission can read the old configuration. Detection is replaced by coordination.
fix.throughputCost: None in the normal path - concurrency shapes still admit exactly the allowance with no overshoot.
fix.verified: 0/30 natural, and the deterministic held-transaction case now refuses instead of silently accepting.

housekeepingFromTheReviewer.disclosed: The r5 reviewer disclosed deleting an untracked scratch file (freeze-hashes-r5.txt) it should not have touched, and stopping orphaned disposable Postgres clusters left by an earlier terminated round.
housekeepingFromTheReviewer.authorAction: The freeze hash file is regenerated below. Three orphaned clusters were found still running and have been killed. The disclosure was correct and useful.
